cards.text: Friend, the LORD has just been talking about Cyrus, king of Persia, setting His exiles free. Now He keeps going, through the prophet Isaiah. He says the products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, along with the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you and be yours.

cards.question: The LORD says these nations will trudge behind you and come over in chains. Then what will they do?
The LORD says the nations who come over will confess that God is with you and that there is no other God.

cards.text: Then comes a line spoken straight to God: "Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior." I spent YEARS hidden in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and not one person ever called me a savior.

cards.question: Now for the makers of idols. What does the passage say happens to them?

answers.text: They are honored by the nations

cards.question: But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an ___ salvation.

cards.text: Then the LORD reminds everyone who's talking: He created the heavens, formed the earth and established it, and He did not create it to be empty. My whole planet is one little bakery, friend, and trust me, it is NOT empty, there's flour on every square inch.

cards.question: The LORD says He didn't create the earth to be empty. So what did He form it for?

cards.text: The LORD says He hasn't spoken in secret, from a place in a land of darkness, and He never told Jacob's descendants to seek Him in a wasteland. Land of darkness? Friend, I LIVED there, it's called the back of a junk drawer, and nobody hears a thing back there.

cards.question: The LORD says that He speaks the truth and says what is right.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out: "Come, gather together, and draw near, you fugitives from the nations." Fugitives, come here. Friend, when somebody yells that, you usually RUN, but this time you're being invited in.

cards.question: The LORD calls some people ignorant. Who are they?

answers.text: Those who carry idols of wood

cards.text: They carry the idol around, then pray to a god that cannot save. That's like me lugging a cookie box across the bakery and then asking the BOX to carry ME.

cards.question: The LORD tells them to speak up and present their case. Then He asks who foretold this long ago. What's His answer?

answers.text: It was the wise of Egypt

cards.question: In that same speech, the LORD calls Himself a righteous God and Savior.

cards.text: Now comes the invitation this whole thing has been building to. Lean in, friend.

cards.question: The LORD says, "Turn to Me and be saved." Who is He calling?

answers.text: All the ends of the earth
The rulers of Egypt and Cush

cards.text: Then the LORD swears an oath by Himself, a word that will not be revoked. Me? I promise a batch in ten minutes and my oven revokes that promise EVERY single time.

cards.question: The LORD swears: Every ___ will bow before Me, every ___ will swear allegiance.
The LORD says that surely they will say something about Him. What will they say?

answers.text: In the LORD alone are righteousness and strength
In the LORD alone are riches and honor
In the LORD alone are rest and safety

cards.question: Everyone who rages against the LORD will stay far away from Him.
The passage ends: In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be ___ and will exult.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 7 quotes "Turn to Me and be saved.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card never says who the LORD is speaking to. It keeps the bare "you" from 45:14 ("will come over to you and be yours"), so a baker could read "you" as themselves. The passage makes the addressee clear in 45:17, where "you" is Israel, and that is something the card may fill in. Card 2 then builds its question on the same unexplained "you".

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card states two facts from outside the passage: the LORD has been talking about Cyrus setting His exiles free (Isaiah 45:13), and Cyrus is king of Persia (for example Isaiah 45:1 and Ezra 1:1). Neither fact has a reference. The card cites only Isaiah 45:14.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The question uses "you" ("trudge behind you", "Bow down to you") without saying who "you" is. The opening card never said either, so the question has no context for who is being bowed to.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The joke does not match the verse's action. In 45:15 God hides Himself and is still the Savior. Papa Dorin was hidden because he was forgotten, which is a different action. The punchline, that nobody called him a savior, does not land and puts him side by side with God's title.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. "everlasting" sounds like the Bible, while "uncertain" and "ordinary" do not sound like words anyone would put before "salvation". The baker can pick by sound alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: In 45:18 the description "who created the heavens... He formed the earth" introduces the LORD ("thus says the LORD, who created..."). The LORD's own words begin at "I am the LORD". The card makes it the LORD speaking ("the LORD reminds") and adds an audience ("everyone") that the text does not name.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "The LORD says... wasteland.", "Land of darkness?" and "Friend, I LIVED there...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the quoted line from 45:20, "Fugitives, come here." and "Friend, when somebody yells that...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "The LORD tells them to speak up" uses "them" to point back to people on an earlier card. The question does not say who "them" is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card tells nothing from the passage. It is only a teaser ("Now comes the invitation... Lean in, friend."), yet it cites Isaiah 45:22. The card doesn't move the baker forward, and it cites a verse it doesn't tell.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "The rulers of Egypt and Cush" is close to the right answer. Egypt and Cush are part of "all the ends of the earth", so a baker could argue the LORD's call includes them.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Then the LORD swears... revoked.", "Me?" and "I promise a batch...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong word "hand" fits the second blank. A raised hand is a common biblical way to swear (for example Genesis 14:22), so a baker could argue "every hand will swear allegiance" is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to pick the exact wording of the line in 45:24 ("righteousness and strength" against "riches and honor" and "rest and safety"). It gives nothing to reason from about the meaning. The question's "they" also has no context.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
